a computational method for the inference of gene-regulatory networks from microarray expression data was developed and applied to the Kaposi's herpesvirus system, and that the method can be used in a wide variety of gene-regulatory systems.

developing and applying computational methods to infer the structure and function of regulatory systems from quantitative experimental data.
the development of a computational approach for the inference of the activity of transcription regulators and gene regulatory kinetics in herpesvirus network.
developing computational approaches to infer gene regulation in herpesvirus and the dynamics of the underlying regulatory network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computational approach described here provides a framework to reconstruct the transcriptional regulatory system of herpesvirus and other viruses from experimental data.
the computational method proposed here provides a principled approach for reconstructing transcriptional regulatory activity in a complex network from gene expression data.

the method described in the paper is a principled approach, and it is a first attempt to use kinetic models of transcriptional regulation for computational inference of transcription factors activity in herpesvirsus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a computational method for inferring the transcriptional activity and the kinetic parameters of a transcription factor in the presence of post-transcriptional regulation and synergism.
the proposed computational approach provides a framework to infer the activity and kinetics of transcription factors and post-transcriptional regulators in a single regulatory system.
we have developed a new approach to reconstruct regulatory networks from microarray data and applied it to a real biological problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinetic method provides an efficient way to reconstruct the transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation of a complex network.
it is possible to reconstruct the activity profile and the kinetics of a regulatory network using only gene expression data.

the proposed approach can provide a quantitative and dynamic picture of the regulatory system of a virus, which is important for understanding the viral life cycle and for designing new antiviral therapies.
